evidence.quote: This is in continuation of Head Office letter no.

relationships.scope: Candidate link: the 20 September 2016 circular continues the earlier Head Office letter on two years' weightage of service, which it cites as dated 25.07.2016; the issuer lists the first letter as 22 July 2016 (dispatch stamp 25 July), so the match is by subject.
The February 2017 circular on two years' weightage refers to the 20 September 2016 letter (number 15850) and the July 2016 letter; it adds Ministry directions and does not replace them.

evidence.quote: Attention is drawn to Head Office letter No. Pension-I/3(4)16/7915 dated 25.07.2016

relationships.scope: Candidate link: the May 2017 circular recalls the Head Office letter of 25.07.2016 (number 7915) on the weightage benefit; the issuer lists the first letter as 22 July 2016.

evidence.quote: This office vide letter dated 31.01.2017 had conveyed that a member must furnish the Aadhaar number while submitting claim form under EPS 1995

relationships.scope: The 27 February 2017 letter recalls that the 31 January 2017 letter required Aadhaar when submitting a claim form under EPS 1995 and clarifies how the requirement works; it does not withdraw it.

The 4 May 2017 circular recalls the 31 January and 28 February 2017 letters on Aadhaar with pension claims (the 28 February number 32049 matches the issuer letter typed 27 February) and responds to difficulties reported by offices.

evidence.quote: Aadhaar No. would not be mandatory for International Workers as well as workers from Nepal and Bhutan

relationships.scope: The 4 August 2017 circular states that Aadhaar is not mandatory for International Workers and workers from Nepal and Bhutan, as an exception to the 5 June 2017 requirement for new members.
The 5 March 2018 letter to the North East zone recalls the 4 May 2017 and 5 June 2017 circulars on Aadhaar for pensioners and members; it does not replace them.
The September 2017 circular on change of date of birth cites the 10 March 2017 circular (number 33314) among its references; the earlier 2006 comprehensive guidelines also remain cited.

Candidate link: the June 2014 circular refers to two Head Office circulars of 8 November 2013 (numbers 528 and 529) on contribution on salary above the statutory limit; only one of the two is in the issuer's circulars table.

limitations: This collection covers Pension Division circulars on EPS Para 11(3) (contribution on salary above the statutory limit), Para 12 (pension calculation, weightage of service), change of date of birth of pension fund members, Aadhaar as an identity document and pension claim forms, and pension on higher wages (2006-2024). Jeevan Pramaan life certificates and UAN-Aadhaar linking circulars are not included.

Supersession of 'all the earlier directions' by the 12 December 2006 date-of-birth guidelines is generic and no named earlier circular is in the set; later date-of-birth circulars (2017) refer to letters of 2006-2017 that are not in the set. The status of the date-of-birth rule after December 2017 is not recorded.
The 2016-2017 circulars on weightage of two years' service cite the first letter as dated 25 July 2016 while the issuer lists it as 22 July 2016; links by subject are marked unverified.

The Aadhaar requirement for pension claims (2017) was applied by dates stated in the letters (1 February 2017 for claim forms, 1 July 2017 for new members, 1 October 2017 for the North East); only the 5 June 2017 date is recorded as an effective date. No circular here states that the requirement ended.

The 2018 and 2023 circulars on pension on higher wages refer to Supreme Court judgments and earlier circulars of 2017 and 2022 that are not in the set; they are included as the issuer filed them but this is not a complete history of that matter.
Several older scans (2008, 2013, 2014) have only partly legible headers; their issue dates follow the issuer listing.
Dates follow the letter, not the issuer listing; entries whose letter date differs carry a date_note.

PDFs were read from the issuer mirror on 4 November 2026 because the public site returned 404 for these paths; recorded SHA-256 values apply to those files. Scanned pages are OCR. Issue dates were checked against the document headers.
